http://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/_book/Densities.html#multivariate-normal-distributions

How to simulate multinormal distribution?
houessou madjid <hmad...@gmail.com>: Feb 08 10:46AM -0800

Hi all,
I'm new to TMB. We are working on spatio-temporal model of the population
distribution for which i've already derived the mean and the
variance-covariance matrix. Now i would like to simulate a multinormal
distribution which take account for these parameters (mean and
variance-covariance matrix). But unfortunately, I get an error message.
Here is my code
###################################################
library(mvtnorm)
simul_logN <- function(T,S,r,sigma_0,sigma,Rho,gamma,Lat, Long){
#check that Rho <= 1 and that gamma <= 1
while ((Rho > 1) | (gamma > 1)){
stop('Rho or gamma is greater than 1. Please do check it.')
}
 
#matrix variance-covariance of sigma
sigma1 = matrix(0,nrow=S,ncol=S,byrow = T)
for (Sample1 in 1:S){
for (Sample2 in 1:S){
sigma1[Sample1,Sample2] = (Rho^sqrt(((Long[Sample1] -
Long[Sample2])^2)
+(Lat[Sample1]-Lat[Sample2])^2))
}
}
 
#set up logk matrix
logk = matrix(0,nrow=S,ncol=T,byrow = T)
logk[,1]<-rmvnorm(1, mean = rep(0, nrow(sigma1)), sigma =
sigma1*sigma_0^2*sigma^2,
method=c("eigen")) #equilibrium population size
at t=0
for (t in 2:T){
logk[,t] <- logk[,(t - 1)] + r
}
 
 
##Simulating logN
logN = matrix(0,nrow=S,ncol=T,byrow = T)
logN[,1] <- rmvnorm(1, mean = logk[,1], sigma = sigma1,
method=c("eigen")) #equilibrium population size at
t=0
for (t in 2:T){
u<-rmvnorm(1, mean = rep(0,nrow(sigma1)), sigma =
sigma^2*sigma1,
method=c("eigen"))

logN[,t]<-logN[,(t-1)]+u-0.5*sigma^2-gamma*(logN[,t-1]-logk[,t-1])
}
as.vector(logN)
}
 
nS = 4
nT = 4
LandSize= c(10,10)
Lat = runif(nS) * LandSize[1]
Long = runif(nS) * LandSize[2]
 
logN = simul_logN(T=nT,S=nS,r=runif(1,0,10),sigma_0=0.2,sigma=0.6,Rho=0.8,
gamma=0.5,Lat=Lat,Long=Long)
 
S = rep(1:nS,nT)
T = rep(1:nT,each=nS)
 
distance= as.matrix(dist(cbind(Lat,Long),method="euclidean"))
 
x1 = rnorm(nS)
 
 
 
#####Code TMB

Cov[s2+(t-1)*nS,s1+(t-1)*nS]<-s2lg*exp((distance[s1,s2]*logR))*(exp(2*t*(lg))*(sigma_0*sigma_0-1)+1)

res = your_dmnorm(logN-meanepsilon);
